s: Start the rice. Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils, the tomatoes and 4 cups of water. Simmer 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and thick.
Salt to taste and serve over the rice.
dal.tip: Red lentils cook fastest. Brown or green work too: give them 10 more minutes.

s: In a wide pot, cook the chopped onion and pepper in the oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice and spices for 1 minute. Add 3 cups of water and the bouillon cube, cover and cook on low 18 minutes.
Fold in the drained beans and the salsa, cover 5 more minutes, then serve.
bbrice.tip: Top with a fried egg or a spoon of yogurt if you have one.

s: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut potatoes and carrots into chunks and the onion into wedges.
Toss everything on a sheet pan with the oil, spices and a good pinch of salt. Chicken skin-side up on top.
Roast 40 to 45 minutes, until the chicken is browned and reaches 165°F (74°C) inside.
sheetchk.tip: Save the bones in the freezer for soup later.

s: Cook the rice ahead and let it cool. Day-old rice works best.
Scramble the eggs in half the oil, then set them aside.
Add the rest of the oil, the garlic and the frozen vegetables. Cook 4 minutes, add the rice and soy sauce, and fry until hot.
Fold the eggs back in and top with sliced green onions.
friedrice.tip: Any leftover meat or tofu can go in at step 3.

s: Boil the spaghetti. Save 1 cup of the cooking water before you drain it.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and grated garlic with splashes of the hot water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, the shredded cabbage and carrot, and the green onions. Good warm or cold.
pbnoodle.tip: Packs well for lunch the next day.

s: Beat the eggs in a mug with a pinch of salt and a small handful of frozen spinach.
Microwave 45 seconds, stir, then 30 to 45 seconds more until just set.
Spoon into the tortilla with the cheese and salsa and roll it up.
mugegg.tip: Works in a dorm or a motel room with just a microwave.

s: Stir the oats, milk, peanut butter and cinnamon together in a jar or bowl.
Cover and leave it in the fridge overnight.
In the morning, slice the banana on top. Eat cold or warm it up.
onoats.tip: Make five jars on Sunday and breakfast is done for the week.

s: Cook the rice. Soften the chopped onion in the oil, add the spices and the drained beans, and mash roughly with a fork.
Warm the tortillas so they bend. Fill each with rice, beans, salsa and cheese, fold in the sides and roll tight.
Eat now, or wrap each one and freeze. Microwave from frozen 2 to 3 minutes, turning once.
burritos.tip: Eight lunches for about the price of one takeout meal.

s: Start the rice. Soften the chopped onion in the oil, then add garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk and drained chickpeas. Simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the frozen spinach until hot. Salt to taste and serve over rice.
chickcurry.tip: No coconut milk? Use a cup of milk or yogurt, stirred in at the end.

s: Boil the pasta. Add the frozen peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain.
In the same pot, melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk until it thickens.
Stir in the cheese, then the pasta, peas and drained tuna. Season with salt and pepper.
tunapasta.tip: Swap the tuna for a can of white beans to make it vegetarian.

s: Soften the chopped onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic.
Add the rinsed split peas, diced potato, bouillon and 8 cups of water.
Simmer, partly covered, about 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the peas fall apart.

chili.t: Stretch chili (a little beef, lots of beans)
s: Brown the beef with the chopped onion, 8 minutes. Add garlic, chili powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste, tomatoes, the beans with their liquid and 1 cup of water.
Simmer 25 minutes, stirring now and then. Salt to taste.
chili.tip: Skip the beef and add one more can of beans for a vegan pot.

s: Mash the bananas in a bowl. Whisk in the eggs, milk and 1 tablespoon of the oil.
Stir in the flour, sugar, baking powder and a pinch of salt until just mixed. Lumps are fine.
Cook ¼ cup at a time in a lightly oiled pan on medium, flipping when bubbles appear.
pancakes.tip: Very ripe, spotty bananas make the sweetest pancakes.

s: Season the chicken with salt, cumin and paprika. Brown it in the oil in a big pot, 4 minutes a side. Set aside.
Cook the chopped onion and pepper 5 minutes, add garlic and rice, and stir 2 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, bouillon and 3½ cups of water. Nestle the chicken in, cover and cook on low 30 minutes.
Scatter the peas on top, cover 5 minutes more, and check the chicken reads 165°F (74°C).
arrozpollo.tip: One pot means one pot to wash.

s: Put the noodles and a handful of frozen vegetables in a big bowl. Cover with water and microwave 3 minutes.
Crack in the egg, poke the yolk once, and microwave 45 to 60 seconds more until the white is set.
Stir in half the seasoning packet (it's very salty) and the green onion.
ramenup.tip: Using half the packet cuts the salt a lot and you won't miss it.

s: Scrub the potato and poke it all over with a fork.
Microwave 5 minutes, turn it over, then 3 to 5 minutes more until a knife slides in easily.
Split it open, top with warmed beans, cheese, salsa and a spoon of yogurt.
potato.tip: Plain yogurt is a cheaper sour cream.

s: Spread the peanut butter over the tortilla and dust with cinnamon.
Lay the banana at one edge and roll it up tight. Slice into rounds for small kids.
rollup.tip: No stove, no mess, about two minutes.

s: Mash the drained beans with the cumin and a pinch of salt. Stir in the drained corn.
Spread on half of each tortilla, add cheese, and fold.
Cook in a dry pan on medium, 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden. Serve with salsa.
quesadilla.tip: Fast enough for a weeknight, fun enough for kids to help.

s: Soften the chopped onion in the oil 5 minutes, then add the garlic and herbs.
Add the tomatoes, frozen vegetables, beans, bouillon and 7 cups of water. Bring to a boil.
Add the pasta and simmer 10 minutes until tender.
minestrone.tip: Frozen vegetables are picked ripe and often cost less than fresh.

sptacos.t: Sweet potato and black bean tacos
s: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Dice the sweet potatoes and onion, toss with oil, spices and salt, and roast 25 minutes.
Warm the beans. Toss the shredded cabbage with lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill with everything.
sptacos.tip: Double up two corn tortillas per taco so they don't tear.

s: Cook the sliced onion and pepper in the oil 8 minutes. Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until thick. Salt to taste.
Make 8 little wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook on low 6 to 8 minutes. Serve with bread for dipping.
shakshuka.tip: Breakfast, lunch or dinner. It works for all three.

tofubowl.t: Crispy tofu and broccoli rice bowls
s: Start the rice. Press the tofu between towels for 10 minutes, then cut into cubes.
Fry the tofu in the oil on medium-high, turning, until golden on most sides, about 10 minutes.
Add the frozen broccoli and garlic and cook 5 minutes. Stir in the soy sauce and sugar until glossy. Serve over rice.
tofubowl.tip: Tofu is one of the cheapest proteins per gram at most stores.

s: Put the chicken, the bouillon, half the onion and 10 cups of water in a big pot. Simmer 35 minutes.
Lift out the chicken. When it's cool enough, pull the meat off the bones and shred it.
Add the sliced carrots, celery, the rest of the onion, the garlic and herbs to the broth. Cook 10 minutes, add the noodles and cook until tender. Return the chicken.
chknoodle.tip: Cook the noodles separately if you plan to freeze it.

pinto.t: Costa Rican rice and beans (gallo pinto) with eggs
s: Cook the rice ahead. Day-old rice is best.
Soften the chopped onion and pepper in the oil, add garlic, then the beans with a few spoons of their liquid.
Fold in the rice until it's speckled and hot. Stir in chopped cilantro and top each plate with a fried egg.
pinto.tip: Black beans are traditional, but use whatever beans you have.

tunasalad.t: White bean and tuna salad on toast
s: Drain and rinse the beans. Drain the tuna.
Mix with the sliced green onions, vinegar, oil, salt and pepper.
Pile onto bread or toast.
tunasalad.tip: No cooking at all, and it keeps 3 days in the fridge.

s: Drain the chickpeas and mash them with a fork, leaving some chunky.
Stir in the mayo, finely chopped celery, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Spread thick on bread.
chicksmash.tip: It's like a tuna sandwich without the tuna.

s: Put the pasta in a big mug with water to cover by 1 inch and a pinch of salt.
Microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring each time, 4 to 5 minutes, until tender. Add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Stir in the milk and cheese and microwave 30 seconds more.
mugmac.tip: Set the mug on a plate in case it bubbles over.

s: Rinse the beans and pick out any stones. Soak them overnight in plenty of water if you can.
Drain, then cover with fresh water by 2 inches. Add the halved onion, garlic, bouillon and cumin.
Simmer gently, partly covered, 1½ to 2 hours, until creamy. Salt at the end.
beanpot.tip: Dried beans cost about half what canned do. One pot feeds a week of burritos, soups and rice bowls.

s: Dice the potatoes small and fry them in the oil, covered for 8 minutes, then uncovered until crisp.
Pour in the beaten eggs with a pinch of salt and scramble gently.
Fill warm tortillas and top with salsa.
bftacos.tip: A dozen tacos for less than a drive-thru combo.

s: Cut the cabbage into bite-size pieces and the tofu into cubes. Slice the green onion.
Warm the oil in a pot, fry the garlic 30 seconds, then add 6 cups of water and the bouillon. Bring to a boil.
Add the cabbage and simmer 6 minutes. Add the tofu and soy sauce and simmer 3 minutes more. Top with green onion and serve with rice.
canhcai.tip: A light soup that goes with any rice meal. Add a few shrimp or some ground pork if you have them.

chaoga.t: Chicken and ginger rice porridge (cháo gà, arroz caldo)
s: In a big pot, fry the chopped onion, garlic and sliced ginger in the oil for 3 minutes. Add the rice and stir 1 minute.
Add the chicken, the bouillon and 10 cups of water. Simmer, stirring now and then, for 40 minutes, until the rice is soft and creamy.
Lift out the chicken, pull the meat off the bones and stir it back in. Salt to taste and top with green onion.
chaoga.tip: Gentle on the stomach and good for anyone who is sick. A squeeze of lime or a dash of fish sauce at the table is great.

s: Start the rice. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Slice the green onion.
Scramble the eggs in half the oil until just set, then move them to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and the tomatoes with their juice and the sugar. Cook 4 minutes, mashing a little. Fold the eggs back in, top with green onion and serve over rice.
tomatoegg.tip: Fresh tomatoes are great here in summer. Use 4 chopped ones instead of the can.

s: Boil the noodles or thin spaghetti until tender and drain.
Meanwhile, cut the green onions into short pieces. Cook them in the oil on low for 8 to 10 minutes, until dark and crisp.
Stir the soy sauce and sugar into the hot oil, then toss with the noodles.
scallion.tip: Top with a fried egg to make it a full meal.

monggo.t: Mung bean stew with spinach (ginisang monggo)
s: Rinse the mung beans and simmer them in 6 cups of water for 30 to 35 minutes, until soft and splitting.
In another pan, fry the garlic, chopped onion and tomatoes in the oil for 5 minutes. Start the rice.
Stir the onion mix and bouillon into the beans. Add the frozen spinach and cook 5 minutes. Salt to taste and serve with rice.
monggo.tip: Traditionally served on Fridays. A little fried fish or pork on top is common when there's extra money.

s: Start the rice. Cut the tofu and potatoes into cubes and smash the garlic.
Brown the tofu in the oil on medium-high, about 8 minutes, then push it aside and fry the garlic 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, a few cracks of black pepper and 1 cup of water. Cover and simmer 15 minutes, until the potatoes are soft and the sauce is glossy.
tofuadobo.tip: Don't stir for the first few minutes after adding the vinegar. It mellows as it cooks.

mujaddara.t: Lentils and rice with crispy onions (mujaddara)
s: Slice the onions thin. Cook them in the oil on medium, stirring often, 20 to 25 minutes until deep brown. Lift half out for the top.
Meanwhile, simmer the rinsed brown lentils in 4 cups of water for 15 minutes. Don't drain.
Add the rice, cumin, 1 teaspoon of salt and the onions left in the pot to the lentils. Cover and cook on low 20 minutes. Serve topped with the crispy onions and a spoon of yogurt.
mujaddara.tip: The browned onions are the flavor, so take your time with them.

s: Chop the onion and carrot. Soften them in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed red lentils, the bouillon and 8 cups of water. Simmer 20 minutes, until the lentils fall apart.
Mash or blend until smooth. Salt to taste and squeeze in the lime juice. Serve with bread.
adas.tip: Thick and filling for very little money. It thickens as it sits, so add water when you reheat.

ful.t: Warm mashed beans with lime and garlic (ful)
s: Put the beans with half their liquid in a bowl or pot and warm them, 3 minutes in the microwave or 5 on the stove.
Mash roughly with the crushed garlic, cumin, lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Drizzle with the oil and eat with bread. Add chopped tomato, onion or a boiled egg if you have them.
ful.tip: Fava beans are traditional. Pinto, kidney or chickpeas all work.

s: Rinse the mung beans and the rice. Simmer the mung beans in 3 cups of water for 15 minutes.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil until golden, then add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the rice, the onions, 1 teaspoon of salt and 2 more cups of water to the beans. Cover and cook on low 20 minutes until soft and a little sticky. Serve with yogurt.
kichiri.tip: Stir a little dried mint or garlic into the yogurt the way it's served at home.

s: Soften the chopped onion in the oil 6 minutes. Add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, the diced potatoes, the drained chickpeas, the bouillon and 7 cups of water.
Simmer 25 minutes until the potatoes are soft. Salt to taste, top with cilantro and serve with bread for dipping.
shorwa.tip: Tear the bread into the bowl and pour the soup over it, the traditional way.

s: Season the chicken with salt, cumin and curry powder. Brown it in the oil in a big pot, 4 minutes a side. Set aside.
Cook the chopped onion 6 minutes, then add the garlic, tomato paste and cinnamon for 1 minute. Stir in the rinsed rice.
Add 3 cups of water and the bouillon, set the chicken on top, cover and cook on low 30 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F (74°C). Serve with a banana on the side.
bariis.tip: A banana with rice is how many Somali families eat it. Try it before you skip it.

diripwa.t: Haitian rice and beans (diri ak pwa)
s: Drain the beans but keep their liquid. Blend or mash the garlic, half the green onions and a pinch of salt with the lime juice. This is a quick epis.
Fry the chopped onion and the epis in the oil 3 minutes. Add the beans and fry 3 more minutes.
Add the bean liquid plus water to make 4 cups, and the bouillon. Bring to a boil, stir in the rinsed rice, cover and cook on low 20 minutes. Top with the rest of the green onions.
diripwa.tip: Red kidney beans are classic. Black or pinto beans work too.

s: Start the rice. Chop the cabbage, carrots and onion.
Fry the onion and garlic in the oil 4 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the cabbage, carrots, spinach, bouillon and 1½ cups of water. Cover and simmer 25 minutes, mashing the vegetables as they soften. Salt to taste and serve over rice.
legim.tip: Add a little chicken or beef if you have it. It's just as good without.

grechka.t: Buckwheat with onion, carrot and egg (grechka)
s: Rinse the buckwheat. Put it in a pot with 2½ cups of water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, fry the chopped onion and grated carrot in the butter until soft and golden. Boil or fry the eggs.
Stir the vegetables into the buckwheat and serve with an egg on each plate.
grechka.tip: Leftover buckwheat with milk and a little sugar is a classic breakfast.

s: Soften the chopped onion and grated carrot in the oil 6 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add 8 cups of water, the bouillon and the diced potatoes. Simmer 10 minutes, then add the shredded cabbage and simmer 10 more.
Add the beets cut into strips with their juice, the garlic and the vinegar. Simmer 5 minutes. Salt to taste and serve with a spoon of yogurt.
borscht.tip: Plain yogurt stands in for sour cream. Borscht tastes even better the next day.

kimchirice.t: Kimchi fried rice with egg (kimchi bokkeumbap)
s: Cook the rice ahead. Cold, day-old rice fries best. Chop the kimchi.
Fry the kimchi in the oil 3 minutes. Add the rice, the soy sauce, the sugar and a splash of kimchi juice and fry until hot.
Fry the eggs. Serve each bowl with an egg on top and sliced green onion.
kimchirice.tip: Older, sour kimchi is the best kind for this.

s: Beat the eggs in a large mug or bowl with ⅓ cup of water, the soy sauce and a little sliced green onion.
Cover loosely and microwave 1 minute. Stir gently.
Microwave 30 to 60 seconds more, until puffed and just set. Eat with rice.
gyeranjjim.tip: Use a big bowl. It rises a lot, then settles.

s: Soften the chopped onion and garlic in 2 tablespoons of the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes, the bouillon and 7 cups of water. Simmer 20 minutes, then mash until mostly smooth.
Stir in the very finely shredded cabbage or kale and cook 5 minutes. Salt to taste and drizzle with the last of the oil.
caldoverde.tip: Slice in a little sausage if you have some. That's how it's served at parties.

s: Break the thin noodles into short pieces. Fry them in the oil on medium, stirring, until golden brown, about 4 minutes.
Blend or finely chop the onion and garlic and add them with the tomato sauce. Cook 2 minutes.
Add 6 cups of water and the bouillon. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the noodles are soft.
fideo.tip: Squeeze in lime and add a little chopped cilantro at the table.
